**Provinces/territories that satisfy all three criteria (based on official Government‑of‑Canada data)**  

| Jurisdiction | GHG emissions 2005 → 2023 (↓ %) | Terrestrial area conserved 2025 (%) | River‑region with ≥59 % “good / excellent” sites (2021‑2023) |
|--------------|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| **Nova Scotia** | **–38 %** | **14.4 %** | *Atlantic Ocean* – highest‑quality region (59 %) |
| **New Brunswick** | **–42 %** | **10.4 %** | *Atlantic Ocean* – 59 % |
| **Ontario** | **–22 %** | **11.2 %** | *Hudson Bay* – second‑highest‑quality region (53 %) |

**Why only these three?**

1. **GHG‑emissions cut ≥ 15 % (2005 → 2023)** –  
   From Canada’s *2025 Progress Report on the 2030 Emissions‑Reduction Plan* (Environment and Climate Change Canada), the following jurisdictions showed reductions of at least 15 %:  
   • Newfoundland & Labrador – 23 %  
   • Prince Edward Island – 16 %  
   • Nova Scotia – 38 %  
   • New Brunswick – 42 %  
   • Ontario – 22 %  
   • Northwest Territories – 21 %【source 2025‑Progress Report】  
   Only Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Ontario and Northwest Territories meet the ≥15 % threshold.  

2. **Terrestrial area conserved ≥ 10 % (2023)** –  
   The *Proportion of terrestrial area conserved, by province and territory, Canada 2025* table (Environment & Climate Change Canada) gives 2025 total‑conserved percentages (treated as the most recent available 2023 data):  
   • Nova Scotia – 14.4 %  
   • New Brunswick – 10.4 %  
   • Ontario – 11.2 %  
   • Northwest Territories – 17.6 %  
   The remaining jurisdictions that cut GHGs (NL, PE) fall below 10 % (NL = 7 %, PE = 5.6 %).  

3. **River‑region with the two highest proportions of “good / excellent” water‑quality sites (2021‑2023)** –  
   The *Water quality in Canadian rivers* indicator (Environment & Climate Change Canada) reports the combined proportion of sites rated “good” or “excellent” for each of the five main hydrological regions (2022‑2024 period, used as the 2021‑2023 cycle):  
   * Atlantic Ocean – 59 %  
   * Hudson Bay – 53 %  
   * Mackenzie River – 48 %  
   * Great Lakes & St. Laurence – 25 %  
   * Pacific Ocean – 22 %  
   Thus, the *Atlantic Ocean* and *Hudson Bay* are the two best‑performing regions.  

   - **Nova Scotia** & **New Brunswick** lie within the *Atlantic Ocean* region.  
   - **Ontario** lies within the *Hudson Bay* region.  
   **Northwest Territories** (though it meets the GHG and conservation thresholds) is not counted in either the Atlantic Ocean or Hudson Bay region, so it is excluded.  

Because Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, and Ontario meet **all three** conditions, they are the final answer.
